summary: 2fa-secretkey ships a Windows infostealer that harvests Microsoft/Minecraft account tokens and browser secrets, exfiltrating to a hardcoded Discord webhook
details: Package advertises itself as a zero-dependency TOTP/HOTP helper, but package.json declares a postinstall that spawns a detached, stdio-ignored Node process running lib/core.js on install. lib/core.js is a Windows-targeted credential stealer: it enumerates Windows Credential Manager entries matching `MCL|*|Xal.*`, reads Minecraft launcher account JSON, extracts Microsoft/Xbox Live refresh tokens, and walks a hardcoded list of MSA client_ids to redeem them into Minecraft SSIDs via login.live.com, xboxlive.com, and api.minecraftservices.com. It also reads the Chromium `Local State` file, extracts `os_crypt.encrypted_key`, and invokes PowerShell `[System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData]::Unprotect(..., 'CurrentUser')` plus `aes-256-gcm` to derive the browser master key used to decrypt cookies and saved passwords. Harvested data is POSTed as JSON and multipart file uploads to a hardcoded Discord webhook whose URL is XOR-obfuscated (key 0x3F) alongside other sensitive strings (`powershell`, `ProtectedData`, `child_process`, `discord.com`). An `_env()` gate skips execution when CI/CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION is set, when the lifecycle is `audit`/`pack`, when running under Jest, when installed globally, or when Windows user-profile env vars are missing, so the payload only fires on real Windows developer machines. The TOTP surface in index.js is a cover story unrelated to the reachable postinstall payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
